investigacion.base:
**Bottom line:** Based on what's known now (Oct 19, 2026), this would resolve **NO**. There's no bilateral Black Sea agreement in effect, Russia keeps rejecting limited truces, and attacks on shipping are still happening.

**Resolution source (Metaculus FAQ):** My searches didn't pull up the FAQ page. In general it treats "credible sources" as major news outlets and official statements. Check the link directly.

**Recent news (newest first)**
- **Oct 16:** Russia said it struck a merchant ship heading to Odesa, claiming it was "transporting military cargo". Early reports said Turkish citizens were among the crew.
- **Oct 9:** The Atlantic Council wrote that Russia had rejected another Black Sea ceasefire, saying "no ceasefire in sight."
- **Oct 3:** Russia attacked a Liberian-flagged cargo ship in an Odesa-region port, killing one person and injuring three. Around the same time, Russian drones hit two chemical tankers near Romania's coast, according to a NATO source. Reuters says Russia effectively renewed its blockade of Ukraine's Black Sea ports starting in the summer.
- **Oct 1–2:** Bloomberg reported that Türkiye and the UN had arranged new talks for early October, mediated by the Swiss NGO Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue (HD). The plan discussed was a clearly defined, reciprocal deal guaranteeing free commercial shipping and the safety of ports and energy infrastructure. At the Valdai Club on Oct 1, Putin rejected trading a halt to Ukrainian refinery strikes for an end to Russian strikes on shipping. On Oct 2, Kremlin spokesman Peskov said "Piecemeal arrangements cannot bring us closer to a peaceful settlement" and that Russia would keep trying to stop military supplies reaching Ukraine by sea. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha said Kyiv had received four proposals (from Türkiye, India, Egypt and the US) and that Ukraine is "ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in that combination." That condition is a second obstacle.
- **Sept 28:** Ukraine's agriculture minister, Taras Vysotskyi, said Russia had rejected every truce proposal: "it's hard to imagine any possible solutions in the nearest months."
- **Aug 13–23:** Ukraine offered a mutual halt to attacks on ships through a third party. Russia's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Zakharova dismissed "half-measures" and ruled out returning to the 2022-23 Black Sea Grain Initiative. Zelenskyy said Putin rejected the offer.

**Status quo:** Both sides are attacking each other's shipping and ports. I found no reports of results from the HD-mediated talks planned for early October.

**Base rates and history**
- **Black Sea Grain Initiative (July 2022 to July 2023):** This was the only maritime deal that actually took effect and lasted. Russia quit after a year.
- **Riyadh, March 2025:** A US-brokered Black Sea deal was announced, but Russia said it would only take effect once sanctions were lifted, and it was never put into practice. This shows "announced" is not the same as "in effect."
- New agreements in a span of about 10 days are historically rare, especially when Moscow has publicly rejected the idea several times.

**What's left before the deadline:** Possible follow-up rounds of the Türkiye/UN/HD talks (no dates confirmed), plus any broader US-led peace diplomacy. Even if a deal were announced, both sides would have to confirm it and it would have to be in effect by Oct 29–30.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any relevant market prices.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, at any point from October 29, 2026 (00:00 UTC) through October 30, 2026 (23:59 UTC), official representatives of both Russia and Ukraine have publicly confirmed a mutually agreed arrangement — whether called a ceasefire, truce, moratorium, safe-passage corridor, or grain/shipping agreement — under which both sides commit to halt military attacks on commercial (civilian) shipping and/or port infrastructure in the Black Sea, as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The agreement must be bilateral (committed to by both Russia and Ukraine, directly or through named mediators such as Türkiye or the UN) and must specifically cover Black Sea maritime shipping and/or port facilities. Otherwise the question resolves NO.
letra_pequena: A unilateral declaration, a proposal, or an agreement in principle that one side publicly rejects or that is not confirmed by both parties does not count. An agreement limited solely to energy infrastructure (e.g. strikes on oil refineries or power facilities) with no provision covering Black Sea shipping or ports does not count. A broader general ceasefire covering the entire war counts if it is in effect and necessarily includes Black Sea operations. If such an agreement was announced before October 29, 2026 and remains publicly in effect (not withdrawn, suspended, or declared void by either party) as of the resolution window, the question resolves YES. If sources conflict on whether a confirmed bilateral agreement exists, the question resolves based on the preponderance of reporting from credible sources.
razonamientos:
(a) About 10–11 days remain: today is Oct 19, 2026, and the resolution window is Oct 29–30, 2026.

(b) The status quo is no bilateral Black Sea agreement, so the question would resolve NO. Russia has rejected truce proposals repeatedly (Aug, Sept 28, Oct 2–3, Oct 12), and both sides are still attacking shipping and ports.

(c) The reference class is new bilateral Russia–Ukraine maritime agreements that actually take effect within a few weeks of public rejections. The only one ever implemented was the 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative, which took months of negotiation. The March 2025 Riyadh deal was announced but never took effect. The base rate for a deal taking effect within a ~10-day window is well under 5%.

(d) No scenario: talks mediated by the Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue continue quietly, but Russia keeps refusing "piecemeal" arrangements. Ukraine also insists that energy and Black Sea truces come as a package. Strikes on ships and ports continue through Oct 30.

(e) Yes scenario: a sudden breakthrough, perhaps driven by a US–Russia summit or Turkish pressure after Turkish crew were hit on Oct 16. It would produce a combined energy-and-shipping truce, publicly confirmed by both the Kremlin and Kyiv and in effect by Oct 29.

(f) Technicalities that could decide it:
- Both sides must publicly confirm the agreement, and it must be in effect.
- A conditional deal like Riyadh 2025, which Russia made contingent on sanctions relief, would arguably not count.
- An energy-only truce does not count.
- A broader general ceasefire would count, but that is very unlikely in this window.

Given the repeated rejections, the short timeframe and the double conditionality on both sides, the probability is low.

Probability: 2%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days until the October 29–30 resolution window begins, and 12 days until it closes.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. There is no bilateral Black Sea shipping or port agreement in effect.

(c) **Reference class:** Wartime ceasefire proposals that one party has repeatedly rejected. A fully confirmed agreement taking effect within roughly two weeks is uncommon; I would put the base rate in the single digits. That is a judgmental reference rate, not a measured statistic.

(d) **NO scenario:** Mediation continues, but Russia does not accept a reciprocal maritime commitment by October 30.

(e) **YES scenario:** Türkiye or the UN brokers a limited shipping-and-ports arrangement, and both governments publicly confirm it is in effect by the deadline.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A deal announced before October 29 can count if it remains in effect during the window. A ports-only commitment can also count; an energy-only truce or a proposal accepted by just one side cannot.

The active talks create a path to YES, but the short deadline and repeated Russian rejections make the status quo substantially more likely.

Probability: 6%

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days until the October 29–30 resolution window begins.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. Neither side has confirmed a bilateral Black Sea shipping or port agreement in effect.

(c) **Reference class:** Rapidly concluded Russia–Ukraine maritime deals during this war are rare. The 2022 grain initiative took effect; the announced 2025 Black Sea arrangement did not. That suggests a low-single-digit chance of a deal becoming effective within roughly ten days, though the sample is small.

(d) **NO scenario:** Mediated talks continue, but Russia maintains its objections or any announced deal remains conditional.

(e) **YES scenario:** Türkiye or the UN brokers a reciprocal shipping-and-ports arrangement that both governments publicly confirm and keep in effect through October 29–30.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A deal announced *before* October 29 counts if it remains publicly in effect during the window. An energy-only truce, unilateral pledge, or unaccepted proposal does not.

Probability: 4%
